title: bug: browser e2e publish drives hand-build approval.branch from the workspace HEAD; take the approval from the daemon's /repository/remote/read preview instead
description:
Parent task-0416061566de49939e91bbd6351be79e, whose step 4 is blocked on this row. That row makes the daemon choose approval.branch: `moe/release/<goalId>` when the remote's recorded default is unknown or equals the workspace branch. No e2e lane has a measured default, because the only measurement runs in node-publisher transmit, after the command. So once the parent passes the target from the preview and the command, a hand-built approval is refused PUBLISH_APPROVAL_STALE @ DAEMON_PREREQUISITE (apps/daemon/src/repository/publish-services.ts:99-101).
Sites, measured at e6369896:
- Default-run in `pnpm test:e2e:browser`, all `branch: "main"` and all expecting ACCEPTED: tests/e2e/control-room/deploy-environment.spec.ts:100, deploy-fake-docker.spec.ts:109, deploy-migrations.spec.ts:142, and lane-rollback-incident.ts:182, which deploy-rollback-incident.spec.ts uses.
- Opt-in or live, each using a checked-out branch name: release-approval.spec.ts:158-167 plus its pushed-branch checks, release-approval-live.spec.ts:282 plus its header comment at :55-62, and live-proof-release.ts:~163-190 plus its comment at :169-171.
Fix, order-independent (green before AND after the parent's wiring, so it lands first): each drive takes `approval` from the daemon's own preview, POST /repository/remote/read {goalId, remoteUrl} -> body.approval, exactly as the control-room Publish card does, instead of hand-building the branch. Every pushed-branch assertion reads that approval.branch.
definitionOfDone: Every site named in the description obtains its publish approval from the daemon's /repository/remote/read preview. `git grep -n 'branch: "main"' -- tests/e2e/control-room` returns no publish-approval literal. The whole-tree census is recorded in the completion record.

The four default-run specs (deploy-environment, deploy-fake-docker, deploy-migrations, deploy-rollback-incident) pass under `pnpm test:e2e:browser` at the delivered tree, and the `N passed` count line is quoted. Those runs take the browser-e2e-gate lease.

`tsc -p tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json` exits 0. The opt-in/live drives' pushed-branch assertions read the approval's branch, never their checked-out name, and their comments that pin `publication-candidate.ts:21` as the branch source are corrected.

implementationPlan.description:
The one shared reader. Create tests/e2e/control-room/publication-approval-read.ts, exporting `readPublicationApproval(lane: DaemonLane, goalId: string, remoteUrl: string): Promise<PublicationApproval>`.
- It POSTs /repository/remote/read with `JSON.stringify({ goalId, remoteUrl })` and exactly the four headers step 1(a) names.
- It asserts HTTP 200 and `{ outcome: "PUBLICATION_CANDIDATE", goalId }`.
- On ANY other answer it THROWS an Error that quotes the daemon's body, so a refusal reaches the log by its own code. It never falls back to a hand-built approval: a silent fallback is exactly the defect this row removes.
- It returns `body.approval` untouched. Never reshape it or pick fields off it: the command must receive the daemon's own approval.
- Type it with `import type { PublicationApproval } from "../../../apps/daemon/src/repository/publication-approval-contracts.js"`. The deploy specs already import from that module (deploy-environment.spec.ts:50), so the edge exists.
- It is test infrastructure, not production: keep it to one small function with a header comment. The comment explains that the drives take the approval exactly as the control-room Publish card does (apps/control-room/src/live/live-publication-candidate.ts:20), and that this is why they stay green both before and after task-04160615 wires the target branch.
Run `pnpm exec tsc -p tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json`; it must exit 0.

implementationPlan.description:
The three OPT-IN or LIVE drives. Their pushed-branch assertions must read the approval's branch, never the name they checked out.

(1) release-approval.spec.ts:
- The positive path `landAndPublish` (:165-180) calls `readPublicationApproval(lane, goalId, remoteUrl)` and dispatches that approval.
- Every later pushed-branch check reads `approval.branch`. That includes the opt-in arm at :336 onward, which still creates `moe-release-browser-<projectId>` so the workspace is not on the remote's default, but must never assume that name was pushed.
- The DEFAULT negative arm at :296-320 keeps a hand-built approval. Say why in one comment: the remote is local, so the preview would refuse it, and ingress refuses PUBLISH_APPROVAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_INGRESS before any approval is judged. Keep `preparePublication`'s hand-built approval only for that arm, and name it so nobody reuses it for a positive publish.

(2) release-approval-live.spec.ts:
- :281-289: take the approval from the preview after `descendFromBase` and the contract goal.
- The `awaitPushed` message, and any read or cleanup of the pushed remote branch, use `approval.branch`.
- Correct the header comment at :55-62, which names `publication-candidate.ts:21` as the branch source. The DAEMON'S PREVIEW now names the branch, and after task-04160615 that can be `moe/release/<goalId>`, not the checked-out name. Keep the separate PR-base paragraph true.

(3) live-proof-release.ts:
- :163-199: keep the throwaway checkout, so the workspace is never on the base.
- Take the approval from the preview.
- Add `expect(approval.branch, "the drive may never push at the base branch").not.toBe(base)` beside the existing guard on the checked-out name.
- Record `approval.branch` in `record("publish-receipt", ...)`.
- Correct the comment at :169-171, which says the daemon reads the ref from the workspace HEAD.

None of these three runs by default: they need a real remote or credentials. tsc is their gate here. Run `pnpm exec tsc -p tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json`; it must exit 0.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. One shared reader module vs a copy per spec. SHARED was chosen. The drives' `command` helpers are hand-mirrored per spec on purpose, but this is one new, identical operation at 7 sites. Seven copies of a header-and-assert block would drift, and a drifted copy that swallows a refusal is the exact failure this row prevents.
2. Keep hand-building the approval but compute the branch the daemon's way. Rejected: that reimplements the daemon's authority inside the test, which the global rails forbid. The preview IS the authority, and the Publish card already uses it.
3. Route the negative local-remote arm through the preview too. Rejected: the preview refuses a local remote (admitRemoteUrl), and that arm tests the INGRESS refusal, which fires before any approval is judged. That arm keeps one hand-built approval, with its reason recorded.

planningNotes.risks:
1. The preview may refuse inside a lane: PUBLISH_GOAL_UNBOUND if called before the goal is bound, or PUBLISH_CANDIDATE_UNREADABLE if called before the landing. Call it AFTER landing, as the card does. The helper throws with the daemon's own code, so a mis-ordered call reads plainly.
2. The browser-e2e-gate lease may be held by a crashed seat. Prove the holder is live, and route a stale lease to #governors.
3. The opt-in and live drives cannot run without real remotes. tsc is their only gate here, so state that plainly rather than implying they were exercised.
4. Removing now-unused imports must not remove a symbol some other line in the same file still uses; tsc catches both directions.
